Proposition
[The Generalized Jacobi Identity]

Source: petersen:page-0065, petersen:page-0066 ↗ def:pet-ch2-generalized-lie-derivative

1. ch2:2.1.6For all vector fields $X,Y$ and tensors $T$, $(L_XL)_YT=0$.
Proof

↗ prop:pet-ch2-generalized-jacobi-identity

\sketch On functions the identity is $[D_X,D_Y]f=D_{[X,Y]}f$. On vector fields it is the Jacobi identity:

\[ [X,[Y,Z]]-[Y,[X,Z]]-[[X,Y],Z]=0. \]

For a one-form $\omega $, evaluation on $Z$ gives

\[ ([L_X,L_Y]\omega )(Z) =[L_X,L_Y](\omega (Z))-\omega ([L_X,L_Y]Z). \]

The function and vector-field cases therefore imply $([L_X,L_Y]-L_{[X,Y]})\omega =0$. Finally, subsection 1.2 extends the result from functions, vector fields, and one-forms to their tensor products and sums.

□
